summary: Turn 7. Both earlier Candidates are accepted as explained, pending_work is empty, so I widened the search on the slow Accept path and recorded a new sourced discrepancy. handlePreAcceptReply acts on a reply carrying a higher ballot than the coordinator's: it increments lb.nacks and, once a majority nacks and the replica is leader, calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870). handleAcceptReply has the analogous block but it is unreachable, because the preceding guard returns whenever lb.lastTriedBallot != areply.Ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026), so the following test areply.Ballot > lb.lastTriedBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035) can never be true. Since handleAccept replies with the acceptor's inst.bal (epaxos/epaxos.go:1001-1004), an Accept reply reporting a higher ballot is silently dropped: no nack is counted, the coordinator's ballot is not raised, and no Prepare is issued, so the coordinator cannot reach acceptOKs+1 > N/2 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1040) and the instance can only progress via the executeCommands COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD recovery timer. Submitted action=continue with a new Candidate (disposition concrete_suspicion, preferred_check source_review, priority 1): principal fact F-DECISION, direct behavior B-ACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER, supporting B-PREACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER / B-RECOVERY-START / B-EXEC, activity_classes A1 and A2; obligation_relation_kind recovery. Counterevidence and unknowns are explicit rather than assuming a defect: the greater-than block is structurally redundant, the higher-ballot information is not wholly lost because recovery is timer-driven so the stall may be bounded, and the open premises are whether a higher-ballot AcceptReply can legally arrive concurrently and whether the IsLeader gate leaves a non-leader coordinator any escalation route. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
